title: Trailryx decision record
description: Metadata plane holds typed fields only. Any free text lives in the encrypted payload plane.

fields.x-why: ULID of the record itself, hex. Generated by us, carries no external content.
Isolation boundary chosen by the operator. An organisation name at most, never a person.
Which shard owns the record. Part of a proof path, fixed at store creation.
agent:// URI naming a machine actor. Not a natural person; a person appears only via on_behalf_of.
One execution. High cardinality by nature, which is why this is a sharded store and not a metrics one.
The run that spawned this one. Crosses shards, so causal traversal is a cross-shard operation.
Delegation chain, root first. A user:// URI is a pseudonymous handle chosen by the operator, not a name; operators are told not to put names in it.
When the emitter says it happened. Untrusted: it is their clock, and it is not the ordering key.
When the decision was taken, per the emitter. Untrusted for the same reason.
Our clock, the one we can stand behind. The time dimension a proof covers.
Which state of knowledge the decision was taken against. The second axis of bitemporality.
Set when the emitter's clock disagreed with ours beyond threshold. Recorded rather than silently corrected.
Closed vocabulary. An open one would be a hole through which content arrives.
Operator-assigned importance. Closed vocabulary, so it cannot carry a message.
Which policy was in force. A version label produced by the operator's own tooling.
Money as an integer of micro-units, never a float. Commercial, not personal.
What the agent remembered, by reference. Copying the memory in would move somebody else's content into our metadata.
Model name. The character set refuses anything shaped like an address or a sentence.
Sampling temperature in thousandths, so it is an integer.
Requested output ceiling. A knob set by the caller, with no bearing on who they are.
The prompt by hash. The prompt itself is a payload, always.
Which tools were in scope. Names only; arguments are payload.
Delegation in force at decision time, root first. Same pseudonymity rule as on_behalf_of.
Parent records. Several, not one: a decision follows from a request and a policy and a memory state and a budget.
How the decision ended. Closed vocabulary; the reasoning behind it, if any, is a payload.
A code, never a message. Upstream error strings quote the input, which is how personal data leaks into logs; the text goes to the payload plane.
How long the operation took. A measurement of the work, never of its content.
Token count. A number about content, not the content.
Tokens produced. A count about content rather than the content itself.
Cost in micro-units. Integer, so money never becomes a float.
Which payload this record points at. The reference survives erasure so the chain still verifies.
Size of the payload. Reveals length, not content; needed for retention and cost.
What kind of payload it is, so retention and access can be decided without opening it.
Which key wraps this payload's data key. Destroying that key is what erasure means.
The actual prompt, completion, arguments or document. Encrypted under a per-payload data key. This is the only place content is allowed to be.
Attributes a mapper did not recognise, kept verbatim so nothing is lost. In the payload plane precisely because unrecognised OpenTelemetry attributes routinely contain prompts and personal data.
Position in the shard's chain. Ours.
The link that makes the chain tamper-evident.
Which segment the record landed in.
Recorded per record so the 2030 migration can enumerate what needs re-signing. Agility is schema, not configuration.
Which signature scheme covered the segment this record belongs to.
Which key encapsulation wrapped the payload key. Crypto-erasure lasts exactly as long as this does.
Which mapper version produced this record. When the semantic conventions move, this moves and the store does not.
